chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, do as you did at al-Shajarah, then pray two rakʿahs behind the Maqām, then enter into the state of ihram for hajj. If you are walking, then recite the talbiyah at the Maqām, and if you are riding, then when your camel sets out with you. Pray Zuhr, if you are able, at Minā, and know that it is broad for you to enter ihram after an obligatory prayer, or after a supererogatory prayer, or by night, or by day.

key_terms.أَهِلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: to begin the rites of hajj by entering ihram and pronouncing the intention
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: Maqām Ibrāhīm, the station behind which two rakʿahs are prayed
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the sacred site where pilgrims stay during hajj
key_terms.تُحْرِمَ: to enter into the state of ihram
key_terms.فَلَبِّ: recite the talbiyah in response to the call of hajj
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, when pilgrims prepare for proceeding to Minā

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim recite the talbiyah and enter ihram for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the procedure for entering ihram for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, including praying two rakʿahs behind the Maqām and the timing of the talbiyah for one who is walking or riding. It also states that the time of entering ihram is flexible, whether after an obligatory prayer, a supererogatory prayer, at night, or in the daytime.
